## 'Replication' crises

:::: {.none}
::: {.fragment}
Another 'replication' crisis – terminological confusion?
:::
::: {.fragment}
The term 'reproducibility' has been used as a synonym for a number of different characteristics – reproducibility, robustness, replicability, repeatability, credibility, and trustworthiness [@NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms, p. 2].
:::
[[Successfully rerun the same code on the same data?]{colour="#b22222"}]{.fragment}
[[Re-analyse the same data a different way?]{colour="#1C69A8"}]{.fragment}
[[Collect fresh data and analyse it in the same way?]{colour="#4D179A"}]{.fragment}
[[Using the same data and same analysis but asking a different question?]{colour="#3C6301"}]{.fragment}
[[Asking the same question but answering it with fresh data and a different analysis?]{colour="#3BB8DB"}]{.fragment}
::::

::: notes
Twenty-nine competent teams worked on one dataset and did not agree, but I have not yet said what kind of failure that is, and part of the difficulty lies in the word itself. For years 'replication' covered everything: rerunning someone's code, reanalysing their data in another way, and collecting new data altogether. These are three different operations that answer three different questions, and because all three were called 'replication', the debates about the crisis had people talking past one another for a decade. [advance] Nosek and colleagues list the qualities for which 'reproducibility' has stood as a synonym, and the questions on the slide are the different operations that hide under the one word.
:::

## The data $\times$ analysis matrix

repeatability_matrix()

::: {.src}
@AlipourfardEtAl2021SystematizingConfidenceOpen; @NosekEtAl2025BriefGlossaryTerms
:::

::: notes
This grid holds the workshop's vocabulary, and everything that follows refers back to it. The question stays the same throughout, and what varies is the data and the analysis. The same data with the same analysis is reproducibility, which asks whether rerunning your recipe gives your number. The same data with a different but justifiable analysis is robustness, which asks whether your finding survives other defensible choices. New data for the same question is replicability. The fourth cell, new data with a new analysis, is generalisation, which we leave aside.
:::
